addn_hosts.description: Path to an additional hosts file (e.g., '/etc/dnsmasq/hosts') to append to the in-memory host table. Maps to the `--addn-hosts` option.

cache_size.description: Size of the DNS cache (number of records). Set to 0 to disable caching. Maps to `--cache-size` (man page: default 150, max 10000). Type should be integer, not number.

dhcp_dns.description: List of DNS server IPs to assign to DHCP clients (DHCP option 6). Defaults to dnsmasq’s own address if omitted. Maps to `--dhcp-option=option:dns-server`.

dhcp_enabled.description: Enable or disable DHCP server functionality.

dhcp_gateway.description: Gateway IP to assign to DHCP clients (DHCP option 3). If omitted, no gateway is set. Maps to `--dhcp-option=option:router`.

dhcp_networks.description: List of DHCP ranges (subnets). Each defines a range and interface for DHCP assignment. Maps to `--dhcp-range`. The interface is not part of dhcp-range syntax; instead it should be handled via `--interface` or the `set:` tag mechanism. This schema's representation is non-standard but preserved per instructions.

dhcp_options.description: List of custom DHCP options (e.g., boot parameters). Maps to `--dhcp-option`. Option codes should follow format: numeric (e.g., '66'), or named (e.g., 'option:router'). The value format depends on the option (IP, string, etc.).

dhcp_port.description: Server port for DHCP. Maps to `--dhcp-port` (man page: changes ports from default 67/68 to specified value). Default is 67.

dns_port.description: Port on which dnsmasq listens for DNS queries. Maps to `--port`. Setting to 0 disables DNS.

domain_name.description: Local domain name (e.g., 'lan') to append to unqualified hostnames. If not set, domain-less queries won’t be expanded.

expand_hosts.description: Whether to automatically append the local-domain to unqualified names in /etc/hosts and static-hosts entries. Maps to the `--expand-hosts` option.

ignore_hosts.description: Whether to ignore entries in /etc/hosts for DHCP (only use static_hosts). Prevents accidental overrides. Note: There is no direct `ignore_hosts` equivalent in dnsmasq. The closest is using `--dhcp-hostfile=/dev/null` to read DHCP host info from /dev/null instead of /etc/hosts. This schema maps to that behavior.

listen_interfaces.description: List of network interfaces (e.g., ['eth0', 'br0']) to bind to. If omitted, defaults to binding only to 127.0.0.1 for security. Maps to the `--interface` option.

log_file.description: Log file path. Use '-' to log to stderr/syslog, or '/var/log/dnsmasq.log' for a file. Maps to `--log-facility`. If the value contains a '/', it's treated as a filename.

log_level.description: Log verbosity level (0 = quiet, 1+ = enable query logging). When >= 1, enables `log-queries`. Maps to the presence of `--log-queries` rather than a numeric value directly. Note: dnsmasq's `log-queries` doesn't take a numeric argument; setting the directive enables logging. There is no `log-level` option in dnsmasq.

static_hosts.description: List of static DHCP leases and DNS mappings (by MAC, IP, and/or hostname). Maps to `--dhcp-host`.

upstream_servers.description: List of upstream DNS servers to forward queries to (IP addresses or hostnames). For dnsmasq, this corresponds to the `--server` option. Note that dnsmasq uses `--server`, not `upstream-servers`. The upstream servers specified here are used because `no-resolv` is set, preventing reading from /etc/resolv.conf. Each entry maps to a separate `server=` directive in the config file (equivalent to the `--server` command-line flag). The entries may be IP addresses or resolvable hostnames (though hostname resolution depends on the system resolver at startup). Multiple `server=` directives can be used to specify multiple upstream servers. Per the man page, more than one `--server` flag is allowed, with repeated domain or ipaddr parts as required.
